key_insight: CG-OMatG uses an equivariant, coarse-grained Riemannian flow model with reinforcement learning to generate molecular crystal structures by jointly predicting molecular positions, orientations, and lattice parameters.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical path to faster polymorph screening and organic materials discovery by narrowing the search for low-energy crystal packings.
method: Rigid-body molecular representation with hierarchical inter- and intra-molecular message passing
Riemannian flow-based generation of centroid positions, orientations, and lattice parameters
Policy-gradient reinforcement learning to bias samples toward low-energy candidates
evidence_signal: The model is trained on subsets of OMC25 and CSD and evaluated on the CSP blind test benchmark using COMPACK packing-similarity comparisons to experimental crystals.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of training data, and coarse-graining rigid molecules may be less suitable for highly flexible systems or unusual polymorphs.
paper_title: Riemannian Flow Models with Reinforcement Learning for Molecular Crystal Structure Prediction
